scenes.title: Mass General Brigham / Harvard Aging Brain Lab: Waist Pedometer Clip Beside Longitudinal Tau-PET Brain Scans
scenes.era: 2019–2025, Harvard Aging Brain Study Neuroimaging Clinic, Mass General Brigham, Boston

layout.description: Sunlit Boston clinical neuroimaging consultation room where a Harvard neurologist unclips a waist pedometer at a sleek oak desk beside a large dual-panel PET/MRI lightbox comparing sedentary tau spread against a clean 5,500-step hippocampal scan.

positions.who: Harvard Aging Brain Study neurologist (in crisp white clinical coat over navy blouse)
positions.where: standing beside the PET/MRI display pointing from the clip-on waist pedometer dock to the clean temporal-hippocampal scan in the 5,000–7,500 step bracket
positions.facing: angled toward the 66-year-old study volunteer across the consultation table

positions.who: 66-year-old Boston volunteer (in walking sneakers and quilted vest)
positions.where: unclipping the medical step counter from their waistband and setting it into the USB cradle on the oak table
positions.facing: toward the neurologist and dual brain-scan monitor

props.name: medical waist pedometer clip and tabletop USB reader cradle
props.period_detail: objective 7-day research step counter used in Harvard Aging Brain Study baseline tracking
props.physical_behavior: State-A volunteer unclips compact black pedometer from waistband -> State-B clicks pedometer firmly into tabletop cradle as step count reads 5,600

props.name: longitudinal Tau-PET comparison workstation ('<3k Sedentary Tau Spread vs 5k–7.5k +7 Yr Delay')
props.period_detail: clinical neuroimaging workstation contrasting temporal-lobe tau accumulation curves
props.physical_behavior: State-A side-by-side baseline amyloid scan -> State-B neurologist taps key revealing preserved hippocampal volume and braked tau curve at 5,000–7,500 steps

actions.verb_sequence: unclips the waist pedometer after a week of neighborhood walks and snaps it cleanly into the desk dock
pulls up the 7-year longitudinal tau-PET overlay and traces the flat protected hippocampal curve

reactions.reaction: smiles with visible relief seeing 5,600 daily steps—not 10,000—hitting the peak brain-protection zone
nods confirming tau accumulation slowed sharply despite baseline plaques

scenes.wardrobe: Boston medical white coat over navy collared blouse; autumn quilted walking vest, breathable pullover, and cushioned running shoes.
scenes.lighting: Bright clean New England morning window daylight across clinical oak desk.
scenes.recognition_hook: Clip a step counter onto older adults with early Alzheimer's plaques, and just 5,000 to 7,500 daily steps slow tau buildup and delay decline by seven years.

key_visual.description: a sunlit Boston neurology clinic where an older adult clicks a waist pedometer into a desk cradle while a Harvard clinician points to longitudinal PET brain scans showing braked tau buildup

scenes.title: Outdoor Autumn Tree-Lined Boston Sidewalk: Brisk 25-Minute Evening Walk Crossing 5,000 Steps
scenes.era: Modern crisp golden-hour neighborhood sidewalk lined with maple trees

layout.description: Sunlit brick-and-stone New England residential sidewalk under golden autumn leaves where a 58-year-old couple walks briskly side by side after dinner.

positions.who: 58-year-old brisk walker (in light windbreaker and cushioned walking shoes)
positions.where: striding purposefully at ~110 steps per minute along the sunlit tree-lined sidewalk, glancing briefly at a wrist step counter crossing 5,200 steps
positions.facing: striding forward down the sunlit neighborhood avenue

props.name: cushioned walking sneakers and wrist step-counter watch
props.period_detail: everyday accessible adult walking gear—zero gym membership required
props.physical_behavior: State-A laces pulled snug on front porch step -> State-B brisk heel-to-toe stride down sunlit brick sidewalk as watch ticks past 5,000 steps

actions.verb_sequence: pulls sneaker laces tight on the porch step, steps onto the sunlit sidewalk, and swings arms into a brisk 25-minute purposeful stride

reactions.reaction: energized, unhurried confidence knowing 5,000–7,500 steps captures peak tau protection

scenes.wardrobe: Slate-blue breathable windbreaker, dark walking pants, and white-soled walking shoes.
scenes.lighting: Warm golden late-afternoon outdoor sunlight slanting through maple leaves.
scenes.recognition_hook: You don't need a marathon or 10,000 steps—one brisk 25-minute neighborhood walk carries you straight into Harvard's 7-year protection zone.

scenes.title: Ditching 10,000-Step All-or-Nothing Guilt at 6 PM: Lacing Up for 2,400 Evening Steps
scenes.era: Modern home entryway bench opening onto sunlit street

layout.description: Bright home mudroom bench by an open front door with walking shoes sitting beside a key bowl.

positions.where: checking 3,100 desk steps on a wristwatch, smiling instead of giving up, slipping on walking shoes, and stepping out the front door
positions.facing: from entryway bench out toward the sunlit sidewalk

props.name: entryway walking shoes and open front door
props.physical_behavior: State-A shoes resting neatly beside bench at 3,100 steps -> State-B adult slips shoes on, pushes front door wide open, and steps out into evening light

actions.verb_sequence: glances at 3,100 steps on watch -> sits on bench to slip on walking sneakers and strides out the open front door

reactions.reaction: motivated relief trading 10,000-step perfectionism for an easy 20-minute loop

scenes.wardrobe: Rolled-sleeve button-down work shirt swapped with walking sneakers.
scenes.recognition_hook: Going from 2,800 steps to 5,200 steps buys the steepest brain-aging protection on the entire curve.
